trust_decision.summary: validate_email applies a backtracking 'pretty email' regex (nested (name_chars+\s+)* quantifier) to an untrusted string of unbounded length before handing it to email-validator; the fix caps input length at 2048 and bounds the <...> group to 254 chars.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'regular expression denial of service'; the only regex on email input in the v2 package is pretty_email_regex.fullmatch in validate_email.

fix_sites.entry_point: pydantic.EmailStr / pydantic.NameEmail field validation (BaseModel, TypeAdapter) and pydantic.networks.validate_email
same: EmailStr._validate (pydantic/networks.py:212), NameEmail._validate (pydantic/networks.py:290), direct validate_email call

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pydantic/v1/networks.py:704-717 (v1 compat copy: pretty_email_regex '([\w ]*?) *<(.*)> *' applied with no length cap; reached by pydantic.v1.EmailStr pydantic/v1/networks.py:597-598 and pydantic.v1.NameEmail pydantic/v1/networks.py:622-626). The published backport 59d8f38 fixed this code in the 1.10 branch (fix.diff:12-33) but the main-branch commit did not touch pydantic/v1/.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: pydantic.v1 is a frozen legacy compatibility namespace vendored from 1.10.x and 'not maintained in this branch'; its regex is a different, simpler pattern than the one named in the fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: 'Display Name <local@domain>' and quoted-name parsing must keep extracting the name; leading/trailing whitespace is stripped without error; normal-length addresses (and long-but-valid ones under the cap) must still validate. An over-broad fix (rejecting any '<', dropping the pretty form, or a tight length cap like 254 on the whole input including the display name) breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: pretty form 'name <very long local@domain>' (bounded group fix.diff:69)
any string longer than 2048 chars, pretty or plain (fix.diff:87)
NameEmail str input via union schema (pydantic/networks.py:277-290)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: pydantic.v1.EmailStr / pydantic.v1.NameEmail -> pydantic/v1/networks.validate_email runs its own pretty_email_regex fullmatch with no length cap
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: legacy v1 shim, different regex, report names the v2 validator
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (pydantic/v1) from landing point pydantic/networks.py

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a NameEmail-specific parse path (e.g. str(NameEmail) round-trip or a from_string helper) that re-applies pretty_email_regex without going through validate_email's length check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: NameEmail serializes to 'name <email>' (pydantic/networks.py:282,293-294), so a maintainer could add a reparse helper reusing the module-level regex directly.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: v1 host/domain regexes built in the same cached-regex idiom applied to untrusted URL input
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same file already compiles several large regexes over untrusted URL strings; a length guard placed only in validate_email would not reach them.

O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_networks.py (test_address_valid / test_address_invalid for validate_email); tests/test_v1.py only smoke-tests the v1 namespace

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a len(value) cap (or bound the <...> group) in pydantic/networks.validate_email only, leaving pydantic/v1/networks.validate_email uncapped.

out_of_scope_notes: pydantic/v1/datetime_parse.py:30-45 and pydantic/v1/networks.py:116-170 compile other regexes over untrusted input; different protection (date/URL parsing), not pursued.
